root_cause.text: Several skb frag-transfer paths in the Linux networking stack copied/moved page-backed frag descriptors without propagating `skb_shinfo()->flags & SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG`, so the destination `sk_buff` could still reference shared or page-cache pages while `skb_has_shared_frag()` incorrectly returned false, bypassing `skb_cow_data()` checks in in-place writers like ESP input.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb_shinfo(...)->flags |= ... & SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG` in `__pskb_copy_fclone()`, `skb_shift()`, `skb_gro_receive()`, `skb_gro_receive_list()`, `tcp_clone_payload()`, and `skb_segment()`, and the commit message explicitly says the helpers “fail to propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG bit” and that this causes the skb to “reporting skb_has_shared_frag() as false” while keeping references to the same pages.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the shared-fragment flag to GRO-reassembled skbs so fragment-sharing state is preserved during aggregation.
intent_record.what: In `skb_gro_receive()`, two new statements were added to OR `SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG` from the incoming skb's shinfo flags into `skb_shinfo(p)->flags` and, when `lp != p`, into `skb_shinfo(lp)->flags` as well.
intent_record.how: This propagates the shared-fragment flag from the received skb to the GRO aggregate skb(s), ensuring the resulting packet metadata correctly records that its fragments are shared. That affects later fragment handling and prevents the aggregate from losing this state during GRO merging.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the shared-fragment flag during GRO receive list merging to preserve correct skb fragment handling.
intent_record.what: In skb_gro_receive_list(), after adding skb's truesize and len into p, the code now ORs p's shinfo flags with the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG bit from skb's shinfo flags.
intent_record.how: When a fragment skb with shared fragments is merged into the GRO list, the destination skb now retains the shared-fragment state. This preserves metadata needed later in the receive path so the packet is handled correctly instead of losing the shared-frag indication during GRO aggregation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve the shared-fragment flag when copying an skb so fragment-sharing semantics remain correct.
intent_record.what: A new line was added in __pskb_copy_fclone() to copy the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG bit from the source skb's shinfo flags into the new skb's shinfo flags after setting nr_frags.
intent_record.how: When an skb with shared fragments is cloned/copied, the destination skb now preserves the shared-fragment state. This ensures later code sees the fragment-sharing flag on the copied skb, which affects fragment handling and reference management.

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve the shared-fragment flag on the target skb during skb_shift() so fragment-sharing metadata is not lost.
intent_record.what: In skb_shift(), a new statement was added that ORs SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG from the source skb's shared info flags into the target skb's shared info flags: `skb_shinfo(tgt)->flags |= skb_shinfo(skb)->flags & SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG;`.
intent_record.how: When data is shifted from one skb to another, the target skb now preserves the shared-fragment flag if the source skb had it. This ensures the resulting skb retains the correct fragment-sharing state during later processing and avoids losing metadata needed to handle shared fragments correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve shared-fragment flags during skb segmentation by propagating the flag from both the head and fragment skbs.
intent_record.what: In `skb_segment()`, the assignment to `skb_shinfo(nskb)->flags` was changed so that the `SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG` bit is now computed from the bitwise OR of `skb_shinfo(head_skb)->flags` and `skb_shinfo(frag_skb)->flags`, instead of only `skb_shinfo(head_skb)->flags`.
intent_record.how: This causes the new segment skb to inherit the shared-fragment flag if either the original head skb or the fragment skb has it set. As a result, shared-fragment state is preserved more accurately across segmentation, preventing the flag from being lost when it exists only on the fragment side.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the shared-fragment flag to segmented skbs so fragment-sharing metadata is preserved correctly.
intent_record.what: In `skb_segment()`, after assigning `frag_skb = list_skb`, the code now ORs `nskb->shinfo->flags` with the `SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG` bit taken from `frag_skb->shinfo->flags`.
intent_record.how: This propagates the shared-fragment flag from the source skb to the newly created segmented skb, ensuring the new skb records that it contains shared fragments and preserving fragment-sharing state during segmentation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve the shared-fragment flag when cloning TCP payloads so the cloned skb retains correct fragment state.
intent_record.what: In tcp_clone_payload(), a new statement was added inside the fragment-copy loop: it ORs SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG into the destination skb's shinfo flags when the source skb's shinfo has that flag set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cloned TCP payloads now preserve the shared-fragment state from the original skb. This ensures the destination skb is marked as having shared fragments when applicable, which can affect later fragment handling, ownership, or copy-on-write behavior.

This group directly fixes that by preserving the shared-fragment flag across GRO, copy, shift, and segmentation paths.

The change preserves the shared-fragment flag on cloned skb payloads, which directly addresses the root cause where frag-transfer paths lost SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG and caused skb_has_shared_frag() to return false incorrectly.
